item.title: Evolutionary principles
item.description:
Source: TW

One of the problems in modern mainstream indological historical inference is the ignoring of the principles of evolutionary inference that are applied in biology: the first attestation of a fossil is not the first time or place the lineage under consideration appears.

For example, the first dinosaur body fossils, i.e., bones known to date, are from around 231-233 Mya. However, fossil footprints provide evidence for an early member of the dinosaur line proper from around 246 Mya – a full 13-15 million years before the first fossil.

item.title: History
item.description:
(Source: https://threader.app/thread/1452838561812815873)

I do think history is important, and the failures at writing an objective history for yourself will result in others writing it & robbing you of your past.+++(5)+++ What is meant by objective: when you write for yourself you have to eschew the impulse to fall prey to contrafactual accounts just because they feel good.+++(5)+++ Now this can be difficult for a nation which has an undistinguished past; however, it is not an issue for the H to tell their own history factually as surviving ancient nation, when many of their cousins have been wiped out by the same forces that seek to eradicate them today.+++(5)+++

item.title: Paradigm shifts
item.description:
Source: TW

A few e.g.s of paradigm shifting finds:

  1. A new veda shAkhA with a notable fraction of new brAhmaNa or mantra material.
  2. Archaic medical text replete with material like to older parts of the kAshyapa saMhitA (e.g., its skandopAkhyAna).
  3. A new original yAmala or bhairava or bhUta tantra
  4. A mathematical text with an algorithm of the order of the kuTTaka or even the chakravAla.
  5. An early astronomical text delving deeply into non-nakShatra constellations – this would paradigm shattering.
  6. Pre-AryabhaTTa mathematical texts with the trigonometric ratio of quadratic or other approximations.
  7. A physics beyond that of prashastapAda.
  8. Detailed zoological treatise.
